entities.summary: Alexandros of Antioch was a Greek sculptor of the Hellenistic age, active during the 3rd century BCE. He is thought to be the sculptor of the famous Venus de Milo statue, created around 100 BCE. Alexandros was born in Antioch, Syria, around 150 BCE, and died there at the age of 50. He was a prominent figure in the artistic circle of the time, collaborating with other notable sculptors and artists. His work had a significant impact on the development of Hellenistic art, and his legacy continued through the Roman Empire. The Venus de Milo statue, one of his most famous creations, was discovered on the Greek island of Milos in 1820 and is now housed at the Louvre Museum in Paris. Alexandros's work also influenced the Roman Emperor Augustus, who commissioned numerous sculptures and public buildings during his reign. Alexandros's contributions to the art world were recognized by the Roman poet Horace, who wrote about his work in his poetry. Alexandros of Antioch's art continues to inspire artists and art historians to this day, with his sculptures and statues remaining some of the most iconic and enduring works of the Hellenistic period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alexandros of Antioch was a prominent sculptor of the Hellenistic age, and his work had a significant impact on the development of Hellenistic art. His legacy continued through the Roman Empire, and his sculptures and statues remain some of the most iconic and enduring works of the Hellenistic period.
